name: Iridium Block 1 (first generation, Motorola/Lockheed LM-700A, launched 1997-2002)
note: Validation model for Iridium flares (the three silvered Main Mission Antennas). Not in the roster. Body frame: +Z nadir, +X the INERTIAL velocity (the front MMA faces it), +Y = Z x X (minus the orbit normal: the satellite's right). MMA normals: front (sin50, 0, cos50); right / left at azimuth +-120 deg. Same attitude as Randy John's SKYSAT and Wyant's Astro::Coord::ECI::TLE::Iridium (Z up, Y = orbit normal there).

sources.value: three flat MMAs 1.88 x 0.86 m, 120 deg apart, plane at 40 deg to the body axis (normal 50 deg from nadir), the front one toward the velocity; where each sits on the bus: estimate
sources.source: Size, spacing, 40 deg: Visual Satellite Observer's Home Page, satobs.org/iridium.html ('188 cm wide x 86 cm long x 4 cm thick', '120 degrees apart', 'angled 40 degrees away from the axis of the body'). Front MMA toward the velocity, the others at +-120 deg, the tilt as rotations (-40, 0 / +-120): R. John, SKYSAT algo.txt (home.comcast.net/~skysat, Wayback 2004-09-08) and T. Wyant, Astro::Coord::ECI::TLE::Iridium 0.133 (CPAN: MMAAREA 1.88*.86, MMAPHI -130 deg). Position on the bus (nadir-side edge hinged 0.3 m above the nadir end; the zenith-side edge 1.2 m out): estimate, it matters only for occlusion.

sources.value: triangular bus 4 m long, 0.9 m sides
sources.source: satobs.org/iridium.html: 'approximately 4 meters long and less than one meter in width', a three-sided body. Side 0.9 m: estimate within that bound.

sources.subject: bus
sources.value: body axis to nadir, front MMA along the inertial velocity, no yaw steering
sources.source: satobs.org/iridium.html ('The axis of the satellite body is maintained vertical'). Velocity alignment: SKYSAT algo.txt (x = ECI velocity, y = r x v, z = x x y) and Wyant's module (same); both predicted flares to seconds for two decades. Adopted from the predictors, not from Motorola.

sources.value: two 1.0 x 2.0 m wings at the zenith end, cross-track, one-axis Sun tracking about the cross-track axis
sources.source: Wikipedia (Iridium satellite constellation) infobox: '2 deployable solar panels'; KeepTrack LM-700 bus table: 'Box + 2 Pan', span 5 m. Size, mounting and tracking law are estimates; they matter only away from MMA flares.

sources.subject: gateway_antennas
sources.value: nadir-end feeder / crosslink antenna cluster as a 0.5 m white cylinder
sources.source: Wikipedia (Iridium satellite constellation): Ka-band crosslink and gateway antennas. Shape, finish: estimate.

sources.subject: mma_silver_teflon
sources.value: second-surface silvered FEP mirror: F0 0.88, diffuse 0.02, GGX roughness 0.0005
sources.source: Coating: satobs.org/iridium.html ('aluminum flat plates ... treated with silver-coated Teflon'). Silvered FEP solar absorptance ~0.08-0.10 (Gilmore, Spacecraft Thermal Control Handbook vol. 1, thermal-control finishes; Sheldahl Red Book): total reflectance ~0.9, nearly all specular -> F0 0.88. Roughness: near-mirror; no measured value found, so the Sun's disc (SUN_ALPHA) sets the lobe width.
Bus and MMA-back finish not published; photographs show a foil-covered body (estimate).

sources.subject: mma_silver_teflon
sources.value: haze: 0.3 of the specular reflectance in a second GGX lobe of roughness 0.04
sources.source: Fitted to the off-axis tail of the Ron Lee / Randy John magnitude-vs-mirror-angle data (SKYSAT iridrpt.txt, 1997, Wayback) and Wyant's ln(8 - m) fit to it (fitted as an area split of the panel before materials had a haze lobe: the same reflectance). Held out: the MMT-9 IRIDIUM 13 flare wing (2015-06-05), the peak magnitude and the footprint.
